risks.risk: The item may be engine mounting parts/insulators rather than a complete engine; pricing for a working engine would be wrong.
risks.proof: Ask for a photo showing the full engine (engine block + cylinder head) and a clear view of engine ID/plate/stamped numbers; if it’s mounts only, ask for a full spread photo of all pieces included.
risks.if_unproven: Price as worn/unknown-fit engine mounting parts (worst case: not serviceable and not guaranteed for fit), not as a working engine.

risks.risk: Condition risk: rubber bushings/insulators may be cracked, hardened, or torn; rust may indicate long storage.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of each rubber bushing/insulator (front and back) showing any cracks/tears, plus photos of mounting surfaces and bolt holes.
risks.if_unproven: Price as needing replacement (worst case: rubber parts bad).

risks.risk: Compatibility risk: without vehicle/engine code, fitment is unknown.
risks.proof: Ask for the vehicle make/model/year and engine code it came from, plus stamped part numbers (if any) and a photo of them.
risks.if_unproven: Price at worst-case unknown compatibility (worst case: may not fit).

risks.risk: “No knock/working” cannot be verified remotely without running evidence.
risks.proof: Request a short video of cold start/idle and a sound recording; ideally include compression test/diagnostic report screenshots.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven working (worst case: treat as non-working/unknown).

proof_requests: Send new photos clarifying what exactly is for sale: complete engine vs mounts/insulators only (full spread + close-ups).
Provide engine ID/plate or stamped numbers (clear close-up) and the vehicle make/model/year/engine code it came from.
If it’s mounts/insulators: send close-ups of every rubber bushing/insulator showing cracks/tears and mounting surfaces.
If it’s an engine: send a short video of the engine running (cold start if possible) and any compression/diagnostic results.
